materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure introduces a significant new risk factor not present in 2024: 'server revenue was limited in Q4 2025 by our available supply of products due to Intel Foundry wafer fabrication supply constraints... expected to persist into 2026.' This moves from a discussion of demand/pricing drivers to a specific supply-side constraint limiting revenue, which is a material change in the company's operational and financial exposure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD report revenue growth in their respective Data Center/AI segments for 2024, but the drivers differ significantly in magnitude and composition. Intel’s DCAI revenue grew modestly by 1%, driven by a trade-off where higher Average Selling Prices (ASPs) from high-core-count products offset a decrease in volume. In contrast, AMD’s Data Center segment experienced explosive 94% revenue growth, driven by strong sales volume of both Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs, without mentioning a volume decline.

sentences.text: DCAI revenue increased 1% from 2023 driven by higher server revenue primarily from high core count products, which increased ASPs and lowered volume compared to 2023.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Semiconductor Solutions segment operating income drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating income from the semiconductor solutions segment increased, primarily driven by revenue growth from networking products (including AI networking products), partially offset by lower net revenue from broadband and server storage products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom identify AI-related products as key drivers of revenue growth in their data center or semiconductor solutions segments for 2024. Intel attributes its DCAI growth to 'high core count products' which increased ASPs, while Broadcom attributes its semiconductor solutions operating income and revenue increase specifically to 'AI networking products'. Both disclosures highlight the positive financial impact of AI infrastructure demand, though Intel's data center segment overall saw only 1% growth whereas Broadcom's segment saw increased operating income.

sentences.text: DCAI revenue increased 1% from 2023 driven by higher server revenue primarily from high core count products, which increased ASPs and lowered volume compared to 2023.

Operating income from our semiconductor solutions segment increased mainly driven by revenue growth from networking products, primarily AI networking products, partially offset by lower net revenue from our broadband and server storage products.

comparisons.peer_summary: Total revenue for 2024 increased 62% compared to 2023, driven by a 60% increase in DRAM sales (due to mid-40% bit shipment growth and low-teen ASP growth) and a 72% increase in NAND sales (due to low-30% bit shipment growth and low-30% ASP growth).
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose that their respective memory or server-related revenues in 2024 were driven by increases in both ASPs and volume (bit shipments). Intel’s DCAI segment saw increased ASPs from high-core-count products which lowered volume, while Micron’s total revenue (DRAM and NAND) increased 62% driven by mid-40% DRAM bit shipment growth and low-teen ASP growth, as well as low-30% NAND bit shipment and ASP growth. While both mention ASP and volume dynamics, Intel highlights a volume decrease in its server segment, whereas Micron highlights broad volume increases across DRAM and NAND.
